source_refs.note: Topic 10.19 with Figure 10.11 and the sample problem, printed pages 235-236. The printed result -0.78 V is recomputed as -0.79 V and both are shown.

blocks.text: For a cell made from a silver/silver ion electrode and a copper/copper(II) ion electrode the reaction is Cu(s) + 2Ag+(aq) giving Cu2+(aq) + 2Ag(s), E standard = +0.46 V. Plotting E cell against the logarithm of the silver ion concentration gives the graph of Figure 10.11: increasing the silver ion concentration makes E cell more positive. The effect of concentration and temperature on E cell is given by the Nernst equation; for a given electrode, such as Cu(s)/Cu2+(aq), E = E standard + (RT / zF) ln([oxidised form] / [reduced form]), where E is the electrode potential under non-standard conditions, E standard the standard electrode potential, R the gas constant 8.314 J K-1 mol-1, T the kelvin temperature, z the number of electrons transferred, F the Faraday constant in C mol-1, ln the natural logarithm, and [oxidised] and [reduced] the concentrations of the oxidised and reduced forms in the half-equation.

blocks.alt: A graph of E cell (0 to 0.5 V) against log[Ag+] (from -8 to 0) for Cu + 2Ag+ -> Cu2+ + 2Ag with [Cu2+] = 1. The straight line rises to 0.46 V, E standard, at [Ag+] = 1 and falls by 0.059 V for every tenfold fall in [Ag+], reaching zero near log[Ag+] = -8. A box gives E cell = 0.46 + 0.059 log[Ag+].
blocks.caption: E cell rises as the concentration of silver ions increases (original diagram after Figure 10.11).

blocks.text: For a metal/metal ion electrode the equation simplifies: ln x = 2.303 log10 x, and at standard temperature R, T and F are constant, so E = E standard + (0.059 / z) log([oxidised form] / [reduced form]).

blocks.title: Nernst equation
blocks.text: E = E standard + (RT / zF) ln([oxidised] / [reduced]), or at 298 K E = E standard + (0.059 / z) log([oxidised] / [reduced]).
Sample problem: zinc in 0.1 M Zn2+

What is the electrode potential of a zinc electrode in a solution of Zn2+ ions at 0.1 M, given E standard of Zn2+/Zn = -0.76 V? Using Zn2+ + 2e- giving Zn: E = -0.76 + (8.31 x 298 / (2 x 96500)) ln(0.1) = -0.76 + (-0.029) = -0.79 V. Since the Zn2+ concentration is decreased the equilibrium shifts backward and the electrode potential decreases.
State the Nernst equation and its significance, and find the potential of a copper electrode in 0.01 M Cu2+ given E standard +0.34 V.
